title: quadlet: skip TestUnitDirs when user namespaces are unavailable
body:
`TestUnitDirs` re-executes the test binary with `CLONE_NEWUSER` before its chroot checks. If the environment denies unprivileged user namespaces, `c.Run()` returns `EPERM` and fails the unit suite even though the required namespace capability is unavailable.

Skip `TestUnitDirs` on `EPERM`, while keeping other errors as failures. This follows the discussion in #29711.

Validation on Fedora 44 aarch64:

- `make -j1 localunit` with the issue's `CGO_CFLAGS` and `BUILDTAGS` passes.
- Reproduced the reported failure in a transient systemd user service with `RestrictNamespaces=yes`: the PR base fails with `fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted`; this change skips the test and the package passes.

Fixes: #29711

> Thanks for the PR. Were you able to reproduce the `TestUnitDirs` failure from #29711? You noted `unshare -U` works on your machine, so the new skip path wasn’t exercised. I’m hesitant to merge a skip without confirmation from a host that actually hit `fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted`. Can you get a quick re-run from the issue reporter, or add Fixes: #29711 once that’s confirmed?

Thanks for the review. I couldn’t reproduce this with Fedora’s default namespace settings, so I tested it in a transient systemd user service with RestrictNamespaces=yes. On the PR base commit, TestUnitDirs fails with the exact fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted error. With this change, it skips and the package passes. I haven’t tested on the reporter’s Alpine host, but this reproduces the reported failure path on Fedora ARM64. I’ll add Fixes: #29711.

> @sairex53 Any update on this?

Updated the commit message with Fixes: #29711 and pushed ce7c649. Reproduced the EPERM failure with RestrictNamespaces=yes on the PR base. With the fix, TestUnitDirs is skipped and make -j1 localunit passes. Could you take another look?
